discriminating_test.inputs: Agent builder, sequential, one acc_capped process at a time (T9 is 4.5 GB, plus a 2^28 table). S=~/.cache/upgh (sair/, bin/acc_capped, T9.tab); W=$S/work/<task>. Per seed: `MAXD=15 INIT_LOG2=28 timeout 240 $S/bin/acc_capped $S/T9.tab 31 210000000 $W <tag> <enc>` (the argument order of research/acc/optimality/tail_replace.py; letters x=0 X=1 y=2 Y=3). Seeds, i=12 moves already spent (full line = prefix + printed tail): [b12] prefix [5,12,12,12,12,0,2,6,1,13,11,5], state (YYxyyyyyx, XYXXYYY), enc '9 3 3 0 2 2 2 2 2 0 7 1 3 1 1 3 3 3' (on the 39 road). [c12] prefix [5,12,12,12,12,0,2,6,6,8,1,5], state (yxYYxyyyy, XXYYYXY), enc '9 2 0 3 3 0 2 2 2 2 7 1 1 3 3 3 1 3' (on the 40, 41 and 44 roads). [d12] prefix [5,12,12,12,12,0,2,6,6,8,2,5], state (yxyyyxx, YYYYXyyXY), enc '7 2 0 2 2 2 0 0 9 3 3 3 3 1 2 2 1 3' (on a 40 road). b12's SAC side also answers a12 = (XYXXYYY, YYxyyyyyx), which road [1,2,5,8,8,8,8,5,10,9,7,3,...] (38, peak 37) reaches at move 12, because a relator swap is an exact move symmetry. To use a b12 (y,x) tail t for AC, drop its trailing 15,15 and map each move with {0:1,1:0,2:4,3:5,4:2,5:3,6:10,7:11,8:12,9:13,10:6,11:7,12:8,13:9} (the yx2 BACK map in tools/acc/ops/twin_beam.py). Then append it to prefix [1,2,5,8,8,8,8,5,10,9,7,3]. First, replay each prefix with the pinned core and check it reaches the stated state. If time remains after the three seeds, rerun the fastest seed at CAP 33. Verify every candidate with the official verifier: the AC line (ac-06045), its AC+[16,15] form, and the SAC line (sac-06045). Write {"id","ac"|"sac"} lines, plus one record per seed {seed, cap, maxd, depth_reached, bestAC, bestSAC, ended}, to artifacts_dir/out.jsonl.
discriminating_test.limits: Total wall time at most 900 s. At most 240 s per acc_capped call, one call at a time. BUDGET 210000000 and INIT_LOG2=28 (29 restarted the container: Playbook memory note). CAP 31 (33 only in leftover time). No beams, no submissions, no push. Write only in artifacts_dir and $S/work/<task>. After a timeout, delete only this task's layer files. A timeout or budget stop is a scoped miss, never a claim that no route exists.
discriminating_test.observe: For each seed: the last stderr depth line (did d reach MAXD=15, or did the run stop on budget or timeout), then bestAC and bestSAC as printed. Full lengths are 12 + L for AC and 12 + L for SAC (L includes 15,15). For b12, also 12 + (L_SAC - 2) as the AC length of the a12 twin line.

result.summary: Every tool that has run on ac-06045 (36, k2; sac-06045 38, k1) was aimed at our 37-move trunk. Direct beams, the mirror twin (37, sweeps/twin_cap.jsonl), windows, the harness tail, mid-restarts, missed-break restarts, road DP and the cap-32 exact echo all worked from the start or from trunk states (Playbook line 110; IDEAS 09-29 12:40Z and 14:10Z; IDEAS 04:45Z). Charlie certified the trunk LOCALLY OPTIMAL at cap 31, with windows up to 11, head up to 23 and tail from move 13 (charlie/v9/ledger/charlie_surgery.jsonl). The pool cannot close the gap either. I ran a bounded check in memory (4 s, pinned core, no files written): a Dijkstra splice over all 23 distinct ac-06045 roads (kernel/known_roads_20260930T0600Z.txt plus the 13 in ROADS_FOR_KERNEL), with exact radius-1 to radius-3 shortcuts, stays at 37. So splice.py and junction_splice on this pool cannot tie. splice.py's waypoint restarts are mid-restarts, which already failed here. The unexplored region is off the trunk. Four roads leave the trunk and reach total length 16 by move 12 (15 by move 16). That is below the trunk's floor of 17 before its final (yx)^5y ladder. These roads still finish at 38 to 40, through tails built only by beams, DP and windows of 14 moves or fewer. No file shows an exact tail from these states. I propose exact capped tails (acc_capped plus the uncapped T9 finish) from three entry states at move 12. The fourth entry is the relator-swapped twin of b12, and b12's (y,x) side answers it by symmetry. With MAXD 15, one run either finds a finish of 24 or fewer from the entry state (an AC tie at 36, and a SAC tie at 38 through the same search) or certifies that none exists under cap 31. Either outcome decides whether this row stays open.

Settings: MAXD=15, INIT_LOG2=28, BUDGET 210000000, CAP 31 (T9 at ~/.cache/upgh/T9.tab, binary ~/.cache/upgh/bin/acc_capped, built from the current source: src sha256 matches research/acc/optimality/acc_capped.c). First I replayed all four prefixes (b12, c12, d12, and the a12 road [1,2,5,8,8,8,8,5,10,9,7,3]) with the pinned official core.apply_move. Every prefix reached its stated state, so no seed was skipped. Results: every call hit its wall cap before finishing, and none printed a path. b12 cap 31: 240 s timeout, last stderr line d=13 (total 103.9M states), bestAC=-1 bestSAC=-1. c12 cap 31: 240 s timeout, d=12 (54.5M states), no best. d12 cap 31: 240 s timeout, d=13 (101.9M states), no best. Leftover-time rerun of b12 at CAP 33 (125 s timeout): d=10 (24.8M states), no best. No run reached MAXD=15 or the BUDGET stop, so none is a completed search or a certificate. stdout was empty on all four calls, because acc_capped prints paths only after its loop ends and timeout killed it. So there are no AC or SAC candidate lines, and the b12 a12-twin check (via the yx2 BACK map) had no b12 SAC tail to map. The driver script that would verify any path with the official verifier (AC, AC+[16,15] as sac-r8-v1, SAC, and the a12 twin) is in the artifacts dir, but it found nothing to verify. Layer files were deleted after each call, no acc_capped process from this task is left running, and the total was about 874 s. The STOP file was absent at every check, and heartbeats were sent between calls. I submitted nothing, pushed nothing and did not touch the ledger.

Board starts checked: every row (ac/sac-01950 n=5, 02033 n=6, 06796 n=7, 03079 n=8, 06727 n=9, 00106 n=10) equals the made-up MS_n start exactly, no rotation or relabelling. Generator: stage A = 5 7 12 5 6 5 12 (MS_n -> level n-1, a=3), then alternating pumps P2 = 1 (4 10)^a 1 5 12 10 and P1 = 5 (11 5)^a 12 down to level 1 (a = 3,7,...,2^(n-1)-1), one move 13 for odd n, Git's exact AC collapse 6 2 10 1 4 + strip, or Git's SAC collapse 6 2 7 5 12 + a mirrored sac_fast_peel tail (helper r2 = g x^k) on (Y x^p, x). n=4 reproduces Git's AC 55 / SAC 56 move for move. Official replay lengths: AC 107/202/398/781/1553/3088 for n=5..10 (records 80/145/275/532/1046/2071), SAC 108/184/331/611/1158/2230 (records 82/147/277/534/1048/2073). 12 verified lines written to lines.txt (and paths.jsonl). The hypothesis (pre-strip in 2^n + O(n)) fails at the prelude for the first n above 4: at n=5 the prefix to level 1 is already 69 (budget 48): MS_5 -A(7)-> Y^4Xy^3x^4 -P2(3),11-> x^7Y^3Xy^2x -P1(7),16-> YYXyx^16 -P2(15),35-> x^31 Y. The level-2 pump (5 11)x(2^(n-1)-1) is only the last of n-2 pumps; the earlier ones (2 moves per BS cell at every level) sum to another 2^n, so pre-strip = 2^(n+1)+O(n) (2064 at n=10 vs budget 1908), AC = 3*2^n, SAC = 2^(n+1) + fast tail. This is Fable's 09-28 3*2^n literal-run bound; the fast peel removes only the third 2^n, leaving SAC about 157 over at n=10 and 26 over at n=5. No exact shortening of the constants (at most a few moves per level) and no search for a non-literal-run road (r0 changed early, 'lever') were done. Ended by finishing, about 45 min wall.

No segment s_0..s_L is shorter for L=1..21 (L<=10 by root membership in the ball; L=11..21 by acc_disk to depth L-10 meeting the ball union), so head is certified up to L=21. L=22 is a budget stop: 10 of the 12 layers were done (22.6M cumulative states) and layer 11 alone was over budget (on-disk 2.14 GB inside the layer). TAIL: the trivial ball under cap 37 has 188,404,513 states (layers 0..9), with search cap 37 (Charlie used B36/cap 36). No tail s_{35-L}..end is shorter for L<=19, so tail is certified up to L=19. L=20 is a budget stop: 9 of the 10 layers were done (28.6M cumulative states) and layer 10 was over budget (on-disk 2.18 GB inside the layer). Layers grow about x4-5 per step at cap 37, so L=22 cannot fit in 80M states. WINDOWS: (a) uncapped acc_window over all pairs <=14 apart plus repeated states, on this route: pass 1, FINAL length 35, no shortcut, 242.5 s (an uncapped no-shortcut result implies none under cap 37). (b) Independent capped-37 check: exact radius-5 balls for all 36 states, all 330 pairs with gap <=11, no shortcut. Consistency control: all 305 pairs with gap <=10 gave distance equal to the gap. So windows <=11 are certified at cap 37. MECHANISM CONTROLS: from s_13 (head, union meet and layer-9-only meet) and from s_22 (tail, layer-9-only meet) a depth-4 search meets at forward layer 4 and ball depth 9, giving a segment of exactly 13 moves that replays to the right end. This validates the layer-9-only meet I used for the tail; it is exact for segments >=10, and segments <=9 were tested by root membership in ball layers 0..9. BUDGET RULE (my wrapper; acc_disk never aborts by itself, and Charlie's original only tested MAXST after a search finished): budget stop = completed cumulative states >=80M with layers still to go, or on-disk bytes >1.5x80Mx16 B inside a layer. result.summary: Hand construction (ac-03855/ac-04662 y-run cancellation template) attempted on ac-08441, ac-06010, ac-00724, ac-08692, ac-02255, ac-07069 from the manifest starts, every step on the pinned core. The template does not start on any of the 6 rows: the MS relator gives exactly two shortening rewrites (X y^L x -> y^(L+1) needs L=n; x y^L X -> y^(L-1) needs L=n+1), and in all 6 rows the matching y-run sits in the opposite flank orientation, so no single multiplication shortens w (work/orient.py; solved siblings such as ac-04662 n=5 record 15 have the right orientation). Across the 128 y-run rows: 102 wrong-orientation only, 26 right-orientation whose one-step rewrite lands on a wrong-orientation core (ac-02572/ac-04158 -> ac-08441's core, ac-08954 -> ac-02255's core). Exact checks on ac-08441: BFS cap 22 depth 12 (84,535 states) and cap 24 depth 11 (177,654 states) contain no relator with <= 1 x-letter. acc_beam + T9 (t00091 driver repointed) from the start: W 20000 plain on all 6 rows, BEAM_CLIMB 4/6/8/10 and BEAM_H=1 on ac-08441 and ac-02255, W 80000 BEAM_H=1 on ac-02255 (161 s): AC NONE / SAC NONE everywhere; BEAM_P2=1 exceeded the 100 s slot. lines.txt is empty (no route replayed ok). orders_charlie.md not written because the construction does not close as a rule; notes.md lists the exact post-opening states per row and the orientation classification instead. All writes inside research/acc/upgh/artifacts/t00092 (scratch moved to its work/ subdir as the lead asked); one process at a time under nice, each <= 280 s.

result.summary: Replayed the pinned-core prefixes first. ac-07900 prefix [1,4,6,6,10,8,4,9,7,7,1] gives (YYYXXYx | yxyxyyyyy), 16 letters. ac-09689 prefix [1,4,6,6,8,10,4,6,8,4,9,7,9,7,7,1] gives (YYYXXYx | yxyxyxyyyyyyyy), 21 letters. CALIBRATION n=5: production acc_beam from the ac-07900 collapse state, W=20000, DMAX=50, env BEAM_H=1 DIV=0.8 P2=2 QUOTA=16 ELITE=5000 DUAL=0.75 NOISE=2 SEED=101 FREE_DMAX=20, 98 s. It found an AC finish of 57 moves. The full 11+57 = 68 route replays ok on the pinned core via core.verify (peak total relator length 24). It is written to lines.txt as ac-07900 and sac-07900 (+16,15). 68 is above record 38, so it will not score; it only shows the finish from the collapse class is reachable. FIRST-SOLVE ATTEMPT ac-09689 from the 21-letter collapse state: (a) beam W=20000 DMAX=120 seed 101, 358 s, AC NONE. (b) same knobs, DMAX=250, 871 s, AC NONE; the beam's minimum kept length plateaued at 17-21. (c) same knobs, seed 202, DMAX=90, 268 s, AC NONE. W=100000 was NOT run: the 45-minute wall and the 1-process limit did not allow it, since P2 dominates at about 0.7 s per depth at W=20000. EXACT (acc_capped, T9 finish, all 14 moves, total relator length cap C, one process, nice 10): cap 26 CLOSED at 2,877,720 states (depth 48); cap 28 CLOSED at 18,284,368 states (depth 58); cap 30 CLOSED at 111,155,792 states (depth 58). AC NONE and SAC NONE in all three. A closed capped component means no route from the collapse state stays within total length <= 30, including the T9 exact finish. The scope is therefore capped length 30 from this one state. A route needing peak total length above 30 is not excluded, and neither are routes that leave the collapse state before or after other prefixes. lines.txt contains only the ac-07900 calibration route (2 lines); no ac-09689 route was found, so no first solve.

settings.stop_rule: a+b=40 without meeting for G caps 22-28 and S3 cap 30

result.prediction: Null on the target: a prefix of <=28 to G is unlikely because G sat in a large component while the start's low-cap components are small, so the connecting prefix should need large caps and be much longer than 28. Hit would be a capped exact prefix <=28 (route <=40); a miss would be scoped to the caps searched. A shorter-than-84 route was a plausible side result.
result.summary: Confirmed on the pinned core (a0fd6e6) that G=(yyyyyyx,YYYYXyyyx) reaches (x,y) by [5,1,6,13,13,5,3,3,3,3,3,3]. Ran an exact capped bidirectional BFS (own C++ tool bidir.cpp/bidir2.cpp, all 14 moves, free reduction, every intermediate state on both sides <= CAP, full-layer alternation so the first meeting is the exact shortest path inside the cap; self-test reproduces the 12-move finish). No prefix start->G of <= 28 moves was found. At caps 22, 24, 26, 28 the search ran until forward depth + backward depth = 40 with no meeting, so the capped start->G distance is >40 at those caps. At cap 20 the start component is closed at 2,700 states and does not contain G. The prefix falls steeply with the cap, so a <=28 prefix, if it exists, needs intermediate lengths above 30. Shortest prefix to G found: 47 moves at cap 28 (full route 59); 64 at cap 24, 75 at cap 22. Also searched to S3, the state 3 finish moves after G (remaining 9, which contains the G variants at distance 1-3 with their own finishes): prefix 65 at cap 24, 59 at cap 26, 44 at cap 28 (full route 53). At cap 30 (140M-state budget) no meeting up to depth 31+9=40, so the prefix to S3 is >40 at cap 30. Order/orientation variants of G lie inside these balls (inversion 1 move, swap ~3 moves); I did not compute separate exact finishes for them beyond the paid chain and its S1/S2/S3 states. Six full routes replay ok on the pinned core and via core.verify (lengths 87, 76, 74, 68, 59, 53), each with an sac twin = AC + [16,15] in lines.txt. The shortest, 53, is below our best 84 and above the record 40. One process at a time under nice 10, peak RSS ~4.5 GB. Every statement is scoped to the stated caps, not a global claim.

result.summary: ac-03055 (n=4, w=YXYXyx, start total 17): built work/acc_capped_run (acc_capped.c + RUNCAP literal-run prune) and ran exact capped BFS from the manifest start with runs <= 8 and MAXD 46 at caps 18 (closes, 11112 states), 20 (775K states) and 22 (45M states, 159 s): no T9 state and no SAC state reached at any depth <= 46, so no run-limited route <= 55 stays inside total length 22. From the 63-route's states 27 (cap 26, 124M states, depth 18, budget stop) and 11 (cap 22, depth 35) with the 63-route as echo: no T9 hit, no shortcut. Exact capped runs on the same family's made-up lower levels gave MS(1)=7, MS(2)=16, MS(3)=34 (cap 22, budget-stopped at depth 32; all replay on the pinned core), so the ladder 7,16,34,55,89,...,2087 has steps 2^n+{1,2,5,2,4,1,4,1,4}. The MS(3) 34-route has no literal run (max run 4): 22 r1-only moves pump r1 = Y^4Xy^3x into the alternating word (xy)^5 x with r0 = YXYXyx fixed (a=YX coordinates: r0 is the BS relator, r1 -> A^6 Y), then a k+7 tail (6 8 2 9 7 5 11, 3^(k-1), 5) strips (xy)^(k-1) at one move per cell; tails verified for k=2..16. Tested the transfer hypothesis (MS(4) -> (YXYXyx,(xy)^9 x) in <= 39 + tail 16 = 55) with echo BFS: all moves cap 22 depth 40 (27M states, but the k=9 target has length 25 > 22), r1-only moves (MOVE_MASK 0x3C32) cap 30 depth 30 (137M, budget stop) and cap 26 depth 40 in full (9.2M): no echo state met. No route <= 63 found; no generator for n=5..10 written; lines.txt holds only the known 63-route (replays on core and stable_core, SAC = +15 15) so nothing new for the board. Miss scope, the reusable shape and the next search (r1-only word space in the (a,y) alphabet, or r1-only cap 26-28 with a 5e8 budget to depth 39) are in notes.md.

result.summary: Middle-bridge search on our best routes (ac-05598: 40 moves, ac-03913: 48 moves). Both replayed on the pinned core (a0fd6e6, core.verify ok). For every pair (i,j) with gap 15..24, 3<=i, j<=L-3 and both end totals <= K, I decided whether s_i reaches s_j in <= g-1 moves (<= g-2 on ac-03913) inside the capped move graph. Method: exact capped BFS balls from each end (acc_disk, official move table) and an exact meet test, B_i^{<=a} intersect B_j^{<=b} with a+b=T and the split chosen per pair to minimise states. A positive/negative control (control.json) passed 14/14 (T=g finds the route, T=g-1 finds nothing). RESULT: no shorter bridge found on any tested pair, so there is no lines.txt. DEVIATIONS (scoped): (1) literal K=start+6=25 on ac-05598 leaves no eligible pair (route middle totals are 26..53; only s_3 and s_32..s_37 are <=25), so nothing was tested there; I ran K=33 and K=37 instead. ac-03913 ran at the literal K=34. A pair is eligible only when both end totals are <= K, so 'certified' means no shorter bridge at that cap, and the route's own higher states do not count. (2) Pairs were processed grouped by i (largest gap first within each i), not globally largest gap first, because disk was shared and shrinking. (3) Per-ball budgets 3M..30M states; a pair's two balls can total up to ~48M states, above the suggested 30M per pair. NET COVERAGE: ac-05598 K=33: 83/83 pairs certified; ac-05598 K=37: 89/89 certified (4 gap-24 pairs were budget stops at 12M per ball and were resolved by a 30M-per-ball follow-up). ac-03913 K=34: 125 pairs, 115 certified, 10 budget stops still unreached, all on the route tail (j in 39..45, gaps 21..24): (17,41) (18,42) (19,42) (19,43) (20,43) (20,44) (21,44) (21,45) (23,44) (23,45). Those are scoped misses, not claims. All details are in notes.md and the res_*.json files.
